title: Sprite Sheets and Animation
summary: Animation is a sequence of frames shown one after another. This lesson cuts frames out of a sprite sheet, plays them at their own speed using a timer, handles looping and one-shot animations, and switches between animations as a character's state changes.

cards.q: Why should animation time be measured in seconds, not game frames?
cards.a: So the animation plays at the same speed whatever the frame rate.

cards.q: Why must play() not restart an animation that is already playing?
cards.a: It is called every frame; restarting each time would keep the animation on its first frame.

cards.q: What is the difference between a looping and a one-shot animation?
cards.a: A looping animation wraps back to its first frame; a one-shot stops on its last frame and reports that it has finished.
